articles.image_title: Rheinland-Pfalz: COCHEM, GERMANY - SEPTEMBER 20: Workers make a breakfast break during the Riesling harvest at a steep slope viticulture at 'Calmont' of Franzen winery at the Mosel River on September 20, 2025 near Bremm, Germany. The Calmont is the steepest vineyard in Europe. Local wineries claim they are harvesting this year earlier than ever before due to increasingly longer and warmer summers. Global warming is creating challenges for local wineries, including more unpredictable weather phenomena. This September was especially wet, causing many ripe grapes to begin to rot. According to estimates by the “Zukunftsinitiative Deutscher Weinbau e. V.” (German Winegrowing Future Initiative), German winegrowing is facing a historic crisis. It is predicted that 50 to 60 percent of all winegrowing families in Germany will soon be facing bankruptcy. Low wholesale prices no longer cover production costs. (Photo by Thomas Lohnes/Getty Images)
